newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end lower in depressed trading.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end lower in depressed trading.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended lower in extremely thin, lackluster trading as a combination of concerns about the economy and Bogota's rocky ties with Washington continued to weigh on equities.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index slipped 0.11 percent to close at 13,470.98 on lower-than-average volume of 442.9 million pesos, while Bogota's IBB fell 0.95 percent, ending the day at 862.54. Volume in Bogota was also paper thin, with just 451.8 million pesos of shares trading hands.
"The market's situation is due to the expectations of foreign funds," said Emilio Echavarria, of Suvalor brokers.

He said foreign funds were clearly holding to the sidelines, and hedging their bets about Colombia's future ties with Washington, until Congress votes on legislation that would stiffen penalities for drug trafficking and lift the country's ban on extradition.

If the legislative proposals fail to win passage, Colombia -- which was decertified by the Clinton administration as a full-fledged partner in the drug war last March -- could be hit with punitive economic sanctions.
Echavarria said Colombia's flagging economic growth was also weighing heavily on stocks.
Losers in Bogota were led by Banco Ganadero, whose common shares fell 4.39 percent to 261 pesos per share.
Brewer Bavaria SA extended its recent losing streak by falling another 0.49 percent, ending at 4,050 pesos a share, and Banco de Colombia slipped 0.45 percent to close the day at 437 a share.
Brokers said all three stocks had been hurt by selling by small shareholders which had a larger-than-normal impact because of the day's low trading volume.
